summary: Candidate sources for adding Medicaid access benchmarks and subgroup evaluation evidence to the New Brunswick / Middlesex County simulation. CMS’s public state tables offer broad external comparisons; person-level TAF files are restricted. The public CMS data page could not be inspected for schema or redistribution terms, so its dataset-specific access and rights remain unverified. These are discovery findings, not acquired datasets.

sources.title: Medicaid and CHIP enrollees who received mental health or SUD services
sources.publisher: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), Medicaid.gov
sources.geography: Dataset page search result indicates state-level data; not specific to Middlesex County or either hospital.
sources.period: Search result describes calendar years 2022–2023; verify dataset version and coverage before use.
sources.grain: Not verified. Search result lists a Year field; dataset page did not expose its schema on inspection.
observed_facts: The search result says the CMS Open Data API supports filtering, querying, and aggregation; direct API URL and fields were not verified.
This may provide an external Medicaid behavioral-health service-use benchmark, but the available information does not establish subgroup dimensions or denominator definitions.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Inspect the dataset’s CMS API metadata/schema and distribution links; confirm whether state, demographic subgroup and denominator fields exist, then retrieve only the New Jersey rows and record the dataset version, source hash, retrieval time and terms.
limitations: Dataset page returned no inspectable content, so exact grain, fields, data URL and rights are unverified.
State-level measures cannot stand in for Middlesex County or hospital populations.
Behavioral-health service use is not a direct measure of language, disability accommodation or wait-time equity.

sources.title: T-MSIS Analytic Files (TAF) Research Identifiable Files
sources.geography: Medicaid and CHIP beneficiary/service records; state availability varies. County/hospital detail requires file and variable confirmation.
sources.period: Annual enrollment/demographic files and claims; period availability varies by state and file.
sources.grain: Beneficiary eligibility and demographic records; service-use and payment claims; managed-care plan/provider annual files.
observed_facts: CMS describes the files as research-optimized Medicaid/CHIP enrollment, demographic, service-use and payment data.
CMS directs prospective users to ResDAC for access, data-use-agreement and request information.
CMS also identifies a public DQ Atlas for state-level data-quality assessments.
sources.retrieval_next_step: For public-only work, use the CMS DQ Atlas and released state tables as benchmarks. Do not request RIF data under this task. If a future authorized project considers RIF, first confirm variables, state-year availability, geography and agreement requirements with ResDAC.
limitations: Restricted research files; do not treat as publicly downloadable.
Not a local hospital encounter dataset; geographic linkage and variables must be verified.
State data completeness and usability vary.

sources.title: American Community Survey 5-Year Data (2009–2024)
sources.geography: Census geographies including places and counties; use New Brunswick city and Middlesex County only after confirming geography codes and table coverage.
sources.period: ACS 5-year estimates; the official page title lists 2009–2024. Existing project context includes 2017–2021 estimates, so avoid combining periods without documenting the change.
sources.grain: Estimate and margin of error by geography and ACS table/subject; variable-specific.
useful_fields: Language spoken at home / English-speaking ability (ACS table family C16002; verify current variable IDs)
Disability status by age (ACS table family C18108; verify current variable IDs)
observed_facts: The Census page provides the official ACS 5-year developer dataset/API overview.
ACS offers population-level characteristics and uncertainty measures useful for subgroup denominator context, not hospital-specific outcomes.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Query Census API metadata for the chosen 5-year release and confirm table/variable identifiers, geography codes, estimates and margins of error; collect only New Brunswick city and Middlesex County, preserving release period and geography definitions.
limitations: Community estimates are ecological context and must not be assigned to individual patients or hospital encounters.
ACS estimates do not measure interpreter availability, accommodation fulfillment, hospital wait times or causal disparity.
Small subgroup estimates may have large margins of error; retain margins and avoid interpreting unstable cells.

missing_inputs: Facility- or encounter-level outcomes stratified by preferred language, disability/accommodation need, race/ethnicity and payer, with subgroup denominators and missingness rates.
Locally measured arrival-to-triage, interpreter connection, accommodation fulfillment and disposition times by subgroup; no public local source was verified within scope.
Verified dataset schema, direct data/API endpoint and rights terms for the CMS public dataset page.
simulation_use: Use Census subgroup estimates and ACS margins of error only to define population-context checks for New Brunswick and Middlesex County. Treat CMS public state tables, if their schema is verified, as external Medicaid benchmarks. Evaluate simulation outputs with five prespecified questions: (1) among simulated encounters needing language assistance, what share has an interpreter need recorded and what share receives assistance, by preferred-language group; report unknown language separately; (2) among encounters with an accommodation need, what share has the need documented and fulfilled by accommodation type; report missing need/status separately; (3) by subgroup, what is median and upper-tail simulated wait time with the same workflow, arrival conditions and denominator, and what are absolute gaps and uncertainty; (4) within each modeled subgroup, what are encounter counts, missing-data rates and excluded/suppressed-cell counts for every metric; (5) does coverage of simulated subgroups align with the selected ACS population context, while explicitly treating this comparison as ecological and non-causal? Do not infer individual behavior from population estimates or call observed correlations causal disparities.
limitations: Two searches and three opened primary-source pages used; CMS public dataset page was not inspectable.
No local hospital subgroup/access dataset was verified in this bounded research pass.
All sources remain candidate leads requiring independent verification and acquisition before calibration.
